info.name: Lab 4 - Breaking and Brokering
info.description:
Team 6, Lab 4 (4.0.0): everything through the Message Broker. Run with the environment deploy/lab4.postman_environment.json (set adminKey from deploy/.env), against `docker compose ... --profile monitoring up -d`:

newman run postman/lab4-broker.postman_collection.json -e deploy/lab4.postman_environment.json --env-var adminKey=$(sed -n 's/^ADMIN_KEY=//p' deploy/.env)

Folders 05 and 07 have a manual step to see the DLQ and the reroute (see their descriptions); without it they check the empty/normal case.

item.name: 00 Auth
item.description: Tokens for the rest of the run. The user is a NEW player registered through the public Player Service route, so the event flow (an exam can be passed only once per player) works on every run.

item.name: 01 Gateway -> Service via broker (Grades 5, 6)
item.description: Every client request goes gateway -> Broker.Call -> one instance of the named service (subscriber-based queue). X-Served-By is the queue, X-Instance-Id the instance that answered.

exec: pm.test("the broker spread the 6 calls over at least 2 instances", () => pm.expect(new Set(seen).size).to.be.at.least(2));

item.name: X-Request-Id is kept end to end
02 Topics (Grades 6, 7)
item.description: The topic catalog of docs/lab4-contract.md §4: the broker and Service Discovery must show every topic with exactly the contract's subscribers (they come from the services' registrations).

item.name: Broker GET /topics: every contract topic with its subscribers
SD GET /topics: same subscribers (from the registrations)
SD GET /topics/exam.passed/services: UP instances with grpcPort

exec: pm.test("every instance is UP and has metadata.grpcPort", () => Object.values(s).flat().forEach((i) => { pm.expect(i.status).to.eql("UP"); pm.expect(i.metadata.grpcPort).to.be.a("number"); }));

item.name: Broker GET /queues: subscriber queues and one queue per (topic, subscriber)

request.description: A subscriber queue appears on the first call to that service; every (topic, subscriber) pair has a topic queue.

exec: pm.test("subscriber queues for the services called so far", () => ["world-service", "exam-service", "player-service"].forEach((n) => pm.expect(q.services.map((s) => s.name)).to.include(n)));
pm.test("topic queues are named <topic>/<subscriber service>", () => q.topics.forEach((t) => { pm.expect(t.type).to.eql("topic"); pm.expect(t.name).to.eql(`${t.topic}/${t.service}`); }));

item.name: 03 Event flow: exam.passed (Grade 8)
item.description: The new player passes the PAD exam. Exam publishes exam.passed; the broker delivers it to world-service (unlocks the East Wing, whose requiredCourseId is PAD) and player-service (XP of the achievements). Nobody calls World or Player directly.

item.name: Admin: the PAD questions with the answers
The player starts the PAD exam
The player answers correctly -> passed (Exam publishes exam.passed)

exec: pm.collectionVariables.set("submitBody", JSON.stringify({ answers: ids.map((id) => ({ questionId: id, selectedOption: answers[id] })) }));

item.name: World: the East Wing is unlocked (poll, exam.passed -> world-service)

exec: // poll pm.variables.get('baseUrl') + '/world/wings': the event is delivered asynchronously by the broker
const once = () => pm.sendRequest({ url: pm.variables.get('baseUrl') + '/world/wings', header: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + pm.collectionVariables.get('userToken') } }, (err, res) => {
const ok = !err && res.code === 200 && (res.json().some((w) => w.requiredCourseId === 'f0000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002' && w.unlocked === true));
pm.test("East Wing unlocked by the event", () => pm.expect(ok, err ? String(err) : res.text()).to.eql(true));
// poll pm.variables.get('baseUrl') + '/player/players/' + pm.collectionVariables.get('playerId'): the event is delivered asynchronously by the broker

const once = () => pm.sendRequest({ url: pm.variables.get('baseUrl') + '/player/players/' + pm.collectionVariables.get('playerId'), header: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + pm.collectionVariables.get('userToken') } }, (err, res) => {
pm.test("the achievements' XP reached the player", () => pm.expect(ok, err ? String(err) : res.text()).to.eql(true));

item.name: Player routes on the same resources stay open
Port 8081 is gone: the gateway registers only its public port

request.description: Lab 2/3 had an internal listener on 8081 for service-to-service calls; Lab 4 services use Broker.Call.

exec: pm.test("a gateway instance is registered", () => pm.expect(g.length).to.be.at.least(1));

item.name: 05 Dead Letter Channel (Grade 9)
item.description: To fill the DLQ before this folder: `docker compose ... stop world-service`, then pass an exam (folder 03) or unlock a wing; after 5 failed deliveries (1, 2, 4, 8 s) the exam.passed delivery to world-service becomes a dead letter. `docker compose ... start world-service`, then run this folder: the retry delivers it. With an empty DLQ the item requests answer 404 DLQ_ITEM_NOT_FOUND, which is also checked.

exec: if (!body.items.length) console.log("DLQ is empty: see the folder description to fill it");
pm.test("a dead letter with its kind and reason", () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().kind).to.be.oneOf(["event", "call"]); });

item.name: 06 Logs download (Grade 4)
item.description: GET /admin/logs/download on the gateway reads every service's $LOG_DIR/<instanceId>.log (shared volume). Admin only.

item.name: ndjson: world-service, level >= INFO, last 30 minutes

exec: pm.test("only world-service, never DEBUG", () => lines.forEach((l) => { pm.expect(l.service).to.eql("world-service"); pm.expect(l.level).to.not.eql("DEBUG"); }));
pm.test("sorted by time", () => lines.slice(1).forEach((l, i) => pm.expect(l.time >= lines[i].time).to.eql(true)));

item.name: ndjson: one request followed across services (requestId from folder 01)

exec: pm.test("every line has this requestId", () => lines.forEach((l) => pm.expect(l.requestId).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("requestId"))));
pm.test("the gateway and exam-service both logged it", () => { const s = new Set(lines.map((l) => l.service)); pm.expect([...s]).to.include.members(["gateway", "exam-service"]); });

item.name: zip: one file per instance + manifest.json

exec: pm.test("every instance has a log file", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().files.length).to.be.at.least(10));

item.name: 07 HA + load balancing (Grade 10)
item.description: Manual step for the reroute: `docker pause` ONE world-service replica, then run this folder: the broker's breaker trips on it and the calls are rerouted, so they still answer 200 with X-Rerouted-From. `docker unpause` afterwards.

item.name: Calls keep answering; X-Rerouted-From when a replica is paused

exec: if (from) pm.test("rerouted away from the paused instance", () => pm.expect(from).to.not.eql(pm.response.headers.get("X-Instance-Id")));
else console.log("no reroute: pause one world-service replica to see X-Rerouted-From");
pm.test("services discovered through SD", () => pm.expect(t.filter((x) => x.labels.job === "services").length).to.be.at.least(10));
pm.test("the broker is scraped", () => pm.expect(t.some((x) => x.labels.job === "message-broker")).to.eql(true));
pm.test("all targets up", () => pm.expect(t.filter((x) => x.health !== "up").map((x) => x.scrapeUrl)).to.eql([]));

item.name: Prometheus: the 5 alert rules are loaded

exec: pm.test("Overview, Message Broker, Logs", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().map((d) => d.title)).to.include.members(["Kahoots Overview", "Message Broker", "Logs"]));
